blocks.text: Condo buildings in Canyon Springs
The Jefferson — 2960 Princess Crescent

(current listings also show units in this complex under 2975 Princess Crescent). Built 1993; one current listing describes the complex as "The Jefferson by Polygon," a low-rise wood-frame strata in Canyon Springs.
The Madison — 2990 Princess Crescent
Built 1993. A current listing for a unit in the building names the subdivision "The Madison" and states the title is Freehold Strata.
Princess Gate — 2985 Princess Crescent and 2995 Princess Crescent

One 55+ community across two addresses: current listings describe Princess Gate as a "55+ adult-oriented community" (2985 Princess Crescent, built 1994) and a "55+ community" (2995 Princess Crescent, built 1993). A 55+ bylaw is the only age-restriction bylaw valid in BC.
Streets, schools and getting around Canyon Springs

items.t: Canyon Springs is a small board sub-area in north-central Coquitlam, on the Pinetree Way / Town Centre side of the city.

Condo stock actually concentrates on one street: Princess Crescent, off the Pinetree Way corridor, where all four complexes here sit — a single early-1990s low-rise cluster. The detached streets around the cluster sit in the City's R-1, R-2 and R-3 zones under Zoning Bylaw No. 3000, 1996.

Anchors on the Pinetree Way corridor: Coquitlam Public Library's City Centre branch, 1169 Pinetree Way; the Lincoln and Lafarge Lake–Douglas SkyTrain stations on Pinetree Way (Evergreen Extension, Millennium Line), with Coquitlam Central station adding West Coast Express commuter rail; Eagle Ridge Hospital, 475 Guildford Way, Port Moody, is the acute-care hospital serving Coquitlam.

Nearby areas: North Coquitlam (the Pinetree Way corridor north of the centre, where the larger and newer condo stock sits), Coquitlam Centre / Town Centre (south), Ranch Park and River Heights (west), and Burke Mountain (north-east).

Coquitlam community medians: Detached $1,455,000, $550/sqft, sale-to-list 97%, DOM 35; Condos & Townhomes $625,000, $687/sqft, sale-to-list 96%, DOM 23. The board does not publish sub-area medians — SnapStats gives sub-area active/sold/sales-ratio but community-level medians only.

items.t: Coquitlam tax timing: City of Coquitlam property taxes run January 1 to December 31 and were due July 2, 2026, with a 5% penalty on any unpaid balance after July 2, 2026 and an additional 5% penalty after September 15, 2026, applied also to unclaimed Home Owner Grants.

blocks.text: Good to know about Canyon Springs

items.t: The whole sub-area's condo stock is one street. All four complexes — The Jefferson, The Madison, The Montclaire and Princess Gate — stand on Princess Crescent, a single crescent off the Pinetree Way corridor, built within about two years of each other (1993–1995). A "Canyon Springs condo search" is, in practice, a Princess Crescent search.

The name belongs to two places at once. Coquitlam's Canyon Springs is a board sub-area; North Vancouver's Canyon Springs is a single Polygon building at 2665 Mountain Highway in Lynn Valley, built 2015. Search results, showing requests and even listing remarks mix the two — verify the municipality on every Canyon Springs hit.

Coquitlam replaced its OCP in April 2026. The City adopted an Interim Official Community Plan on April 27, 2026 (Bylaws 5511, 2026 and 5512, 2026), superseding the Citywide OCP No. 3479, 2001 — any Canyon Springs density or land-use claim sourced to the old OCP is out of date.
The sub-area has market stats, but no sub-area median — by design. Any source quoting a "Canyon Springs median" is inventing a figure the publisher does not produce.
The school answer depends on three tiers, not two.

Creek rules reach further than buyers expect. Coquitlam's Watercourse Protection Development Permit Area applies within 30 m of the top of a watercourse or ravine bank, and Zoning Bylaw ss. 519 and 523 add flood construction and riparian setbacks — relevant to the detached lots around the Princess Crescent cluster and to any strata common-property work near a creek.

blocks.text: Townhome complexes in Canyon Springs
Streets, schools and getting around Canyon Springs

items.t: Where the attached stock concentrates: one street — Princess Crescent, off the Pinetree Way corridor, where all four complexes here sit, a single early-1990s low-rise apartment cluster. The detached streets around the cluster sit in the City's R-1, R-2 and R-3 zones under Zoning Bylaw No. 3000, 1996. Nearby areas: Central Coquitlam to the south, North Coquitlam / City Centre (board naming) and Town Centre Park to the north-east, Burke Mountain beyond, and Coquitlam East to the east.

Anchors on the corridor: Coquitlam Public Library City Centre branch, 1169 Pinetree Way (Poirier branch, 575 Poirier Street, is the other branch); the Lincoln and Lafarge Lake-Douglas SkyTrain stations on Pinetree Way (Evergreen Extension, Millennium Line), with Coquitlam Central Station adding West Coast Express service; Eagle Ridge Hospital, 475 Guildford Way, Port Moody, is the Fraser Health hospital on the Port Moody / Coquitlam border and the nearest hospital for this area.

Coquitlam community medians (SnapStats publishes medians at community level only, never for this sub-area): Detached $1,455,000, $550/sqft, sale-to-list 97%, 35 days on market; Condos & Townhomes $625,000, $687/sqft, sale-to-list 96%, 23 days on market.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect townhome buyers in Canyon Springs

items.t: Form B diligence (the Princess Crescent stratas, and any strata purchase compared nearby): Strata Property Act s. 59 — the Form B states the lot's monthly strata fees, amounts owing, approved special levies still payable, the CRF balance and an insurance summary, with the rules, current budget, any Rental Disclosure Statement and the most recent depreciation report attached; provided within 7 days, maximum $35 plus up to 25 cents per page. All four Princess Crescent complexes date from 1993–1995, so the depreciation report is the first document to read in this sub-area.

Coquitlam zoning and plan: Zoning Bylaw No. 3000, 1996 governs, with small-scale residential zones R-1, R-2 and R-3 and subdivision minimums of 650 m² and 18.5 m width (R-1, R-3) and 465 m² and 12.5 m (R-2). The City adopted an Interim Official Community Plan on April 27, 2026 (Bylaws 5511, 2026 and 5512, 2026), superseding the Citywide OCP No. 3479, 2001, so any Canyon Springs land-use claim sourced to the old OCP is out of date. SSMUH as the City states it: up to 3 units on lots 280 m² or smaller and up to 4 units on lots larger than 280 m² and under 4,050 m², including secondary suites and carriage or laneway homes; lots not connected to municipal water or sewer are outside the SSMUH rules. Watercourse rules reach the cluster's edge lots: a Watercourse Protection Development Permit Area within 30 m of the top of a watercourse or ravine bank, Zoning Bylaw s. 519 flood protection setbacks and s. 523 riparian setbacks.

The Watercourse Protection Development Permit Area applies within 30 m of the top of a watercourse or ravine bank, and Zoning Bylaw ss. 519 and 523 add flood construction and riparian setbacks — relevant to the detached lots around the Princess Crescent cluster (the cluster sits by the Hoy Creek greenbelt per listing copy) and to any strata common-property work near a creek.

Princess Gate's CRF is part of its marketing — verify it anyway. A Princess Gate listing describes a "well-run, proactive strata with nearly $1M in the CRF" alongside its lap pool, fitness centre, clubhouse, guest suites, library and workshop. Listing copy is not the Form B; the CRF balance and depreciation report in the Form B package govern.

blocks.text: Canyon Springs home prices: what sold, November 2025 to October 2026

31 condos sold in Canyon Springs with a median price of $530,000 (the middle half sold between $436,250 and $576,125), taking a median of 19 days to sell at 97.6% of the last list price; 6% sold above list. They had a median $589 per square foot, a median year built of 1994 and a median strata fee of $481 a month.

faq.a: At the end of October 2026 the Greater Vancouver REALTORS® figures showed 24 condos and townhomes listed in Canyon Springs. That is a month-end count and it moves daily; ask Jared what is on the market today.
faq.q: How many condos and townhomes are for sale in Canyon Springs?

faq.a: In October 2026, condos and townhomes in Canyon Springs had a sales ratio of 13%, which the reports’ scale reads as a balanced market. On the reports’ scale under 12% favours buyers, 12% to 20% is balanced and over 20% favours sellers.
faq.q: Is Canyon Springs a buyers’ or sellers’ market for condos and townhomes?

faq.a: 21 condos and townhomes sold in Canyon Springs over those 5 months, out of 596 in all of Coquitlam.
faq.q: How many condos and townhomes sold in Canyon Springs from June to October 2026?

faq.a: No. The monthly reports publish condos and townhomes as one line, so every count here includes both. Jared can pull the split for a specific building or street.
faq.q: Do these numbers separate condos from townhomes?

faq.a: "Canyon Springs" is a Greater Vancouver REALTORS® sub-area name for this pocket of north-central Coquitlam (it appears in the SnapStats Greater Vancouver September 2026 report). North Vancouver separately has a building named Canyon Springs at 2665 Mountain Highway in Lynn Valley — a different place that shares the name.
faq.q: Is Canyon Springs in North Vancouver or Coquitlam?

faq.a: Four low-rise complexes, all on Princess Crescent and all from 1993–1995: The Jefferson (2960 Princess Crescent), The Madison (2990), The Montclaire (2970) and Princess Gate (2985 and 2995).
faq.q: What condo stock does the sub-area actually have?

faq.a: The Coquitlam community median for Condos & Townhomes in September 2026 was $625,000, at $687/sqft, 96% sale-to-list and 23 days on market. Do not quote a Canyon Springs median.
faq.q: What is the sub-area's median condo price?

faq.a: The published listings describe Princess Gate as a 55+ adult-oriented community across 2985 and 2995 Princess Crescent. A 55+ bylaw is the only age bylaw valid under Strata Property Act ss. 123.1/123.2; exemptions cover legacy residents, live-in caregivers and, from May 1, 2023, younger spouses/partners and defined children of a 55+ resident. Confirm the filed bylaw on the Form B before assuming who may live in the unit.
faq.q: Princess Gate is 55+. Can a younger buyer purchase there?

faq.a: No — rental-restriction bylaws have been unenforceable anywhere in BC since November 24, 2022. A short-term rental bylaw can still bind.
faq.q: Can a strata here ban me from renting my unit out long-term?

faq.a: North Vancouver separately has a building named Canyon Springs at 2665 Mountain Hwy in Lynn Valley, built 2015 by Polygon — a different place that shares the name. Verify the municipality on every Canyon Springs search hit.
faq.q: Is Canyon Springs in North Vancouver or Coquitlam?

faq.a: The sub-area's attached stock is four low-rise apartment complexes on one street, Princess Crescent, all from 1993–1995. A unit inside The Jefferson marketed as a "loft-style townhouse" is a unit within that apartment strata, not a townhouse complex.
faq.q: Are there any townhouses in Canyon Springs, Coquitlam?

faq.a: There isn't one. SnapStats publishes sub-area inventory, sales and sales ratio only; the $625,000 Condos & Townhomes median is Coquitlam-wide ($687/sqft, 96% sale-to-list, 23 days, September 2026). Do not quote a Canyon Springs median.
faq.q: What is the sub-area's median townhouse price?
What did condos in Canyon Springs sell for?
faq.a: 31 condos sold in Canyon Springs between November 1, 2025 to October 22, 2026, with a median price of $530,000.

faq.q: How long do condos take to sell in Canyon Springs?
faq.a: The median was 19 days from listing to sale, and homes sold at a median 97.6% of the last list price (6% sold above list), for sales November 1, 2025 to October 22, 2026.
